legalName: Motion to Void a First Controlled-Substance Possession Conviction and Seal the Records (KRS 218A.275)
publicName: Void and seal a first Kentucky drug possession conviction
compositeReliefNote: The statutory remedy is composite: under KRS 218A.275(8) the court may void the conviction, and under (9) it shall then order the records sealed. "sealing" is carried as the single relief noun because it is the operative relief on the records; the voiding is carried as presentation.reliefActionVerb ("void and seal"). No source read for this track supplies a one-word name for the composite remedy.

packetSet.components lists three components: a required primary filing (custom_pleading), a required proposed order that is an official PDF fill of AOC-334, and a required certificate of service (custom_pleading). Lane C drafts the two custom-pleading components and drafts nothing for AOC-334.

AOC-334 is a Kentucky AOC official form with a recorded officialFormId and officialSourceUrl. It is recorded as a mandatory official-form dependency and handed to the official-PDF overlay lane; drafting a substitute order would be invention of a court order.

primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: After satisfactory completion of treatment, probation or other sentence on a first conviction for possession of a controlled substance, the court may void the conviction.
On voiding, the court shall order the records sealed, except as provided in KRS 27A.099.
A voided conviction is not a first offence for later Chapter 218A purposes and is not a conviction for disqualifications or disabilities imposed by law.
Voiding may occur only once for any person, and the subsection excludes a person who has previously had a charge dismissed after completion of a deferred prosecution programme under KRS 218A.14151.
Records excepted from sealing. Records excepted by KRS 27A.099 are not sealed.
The five-year period does not apply where the conviction was voided under KRS 218A.275(8). Carried as a packet instruction for onward routing, not as relief requested in this motion.

counselFlags.statement: KRS 218A.275(12) bars this relief to anyone who previously had a possession charge dismissed after a deferred prosecution under KRS 218A.14151. The controlling legal review does not record that bar. It changes who receives a packet at all. The screening question vcsPriorDeferredProsecution exists on the track, but the bar itself is not ratified as encoded.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That the KRS 218A.275(12) deferred-prosecution bar is encoded as an absolute eligibility bar before this route is built, and that vcsPriorDeferredProsecution gates packet generation rather than merely being collected.

counselFlags.statement: The static legal propositions this motion would assert about the effect of voiding and sealing — that a voided conviction is not a first offence for later Chapter 218A purposes and is not a conviction for disqualifications or disabilities imposed by law (KRS 218A.275(10)), and that the court shall order the records sealed (KRS 218A.275(9)) — have not been ratified by counsel. The motion cannot go out until they are.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Ratify the fixed statements of legal effect the void-and-seal motion may make about KRS 218A.275(9) and (10).

counselFlags.statement: The required proposed order is official form AOC-334, Order Voiding Conviction and Sealing Records, Rev. 1-22, tendered with the motion. Lane C drafts no order text for it. This is a mandatory official-form handoff to the official-PDF overlay lane; the order's own content, including which agencies it names as custodians, comes from that form and not from this config.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That AOC-334 overlay and field mapping is owned and completed by the official-PDF overlay lane, and that the packet tenders the official form rather than any drafted substitute.

counselFlags.statement: KRS 218A.14151 deferred prosecution is an adjacent record-clearing mechanism the controlling review never identifies. AOC-333 is its sealing order and AOC-331 its participant-facing application. Recorded as an observation only; it is not normalized here and no packet references it.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Should KRS 218A.14151 deferred prosecution be added to the Kentucky mechanism denominator in a later edition?

counselFlags.statement: The scope of the KRS 27A.099 exception, which keeps some records outside the sealing order, is an open research note. The motion and the participant copy say that records excepted by KRS 27A.099 are not reached; neither enumerates which records those are.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: The scope of KRS 27A.099 before any statement is made to a participant about which records survive sealing.

counselFlags.statement: No source read for this track states an accepted caption or format. What is sourced is that the motion is made in the original criminal case, is filed under the original case number as motion type SA, that no summons issues, and that the clerk delivers it to the judge who decided the case. The caption in this config is a token pattern built from those facts plus the participant's screening answers.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: The caption and format Kentucky circuit court clerks accept for a KRS 218A.275(8) motion, since no official form exists for the motion itself.

counselFlags.statement: Whether this is a first offence is the participant's own statement of fact and is never generated as a legal conclusion. Any dispute ends automated assistance. The motion states the participant's answer as the participant's own averment and asserts no first-offence conclusion of its own.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That no pipeline stage derives, infers or asserts first-offence status from any record.

counselFlags.statement: Voiding may occur only once for any person. A participant who has already had a conviction voided under KRS 218A.275 is excluded, and the packet asserts nothing about prior voidings beyond the participant's own answer to vcsPriorVoid.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That vcsPriorVoid is an eligibility gate and not merely a collected answer.

counselFlags.statement: Sealing is not expungement. The records continue to exist and are sealed, and records excepted by KRS 27A.099 are not reached at all. The rendered motion must never use expungement vocabulary; qaProhibitedTerms enforces that.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That participant copy and rendered output for this track never promise erasure or destruction of records.

counselFlags.statement: A conviction voided under KRS 218A.275(8) can then be expunged under KRS 431.078 with no five-year wait; where the offence was a misdemeanor the participant should be routed on to ky_misdemeanor_expungement. That is a downstream routing instruction, not relief requested in this motion, and it is stated in participant copy only.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That routing to the KRS 431.078 expungement track happens only after an order voiding the conviction is entered, never before.

counselFlags.statement: Any participant who is not a United States citizen is a self-help stop condition on this track, because a voided conviction may still be a conviction for immigration purposes.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That screening stops on a non-citizen participant before any packet is produced.

counselFlags.mustConfirm: That both stop conditions are wired, and that no fee figure of any kind is quoted to a participant.

rendererCompatibility.note: This config is data. It is written against the PleadingTrackConfig shape consumed by src/lib/record-clearing/renderers/custom-pleading-renderer.ts, but that renderer cannot yet consume it faithfully. The defects below were observed in a rendered sample of fixtures/canonical.json produced in this worktree. They are renderer/adapter defects, not data defects, and no source-faithful field has been altered to work around them.

adapterDefects.observed: Fields deliberately set to null under the sourced-content-only rule are printed literally as the text 'null' — the caption rendered "COMMONWEALTH OF KENTUCKY,\n    null,", the parties block rendered "null is the Commonwealth of Kentucky.", and the verification clause rendered "I, [NAME], null that the statements ...".
adapterDefects.requiredAdapterBehavior: A null role, verb or label means the source does not state one. The adapter must omit the line or clause entirely, never stringify null. Null is the convention this artifact set is required to use for unsourced values; supplying a value instead would be invention.

adapterDefects.observed: A 'VI. VERIFICATION' section was emitted with a truth-of-statements clause, although this track's registry entry states "none required. The motion is not verified." and componentInventory marks verification absent.
adapterDefects.requiredAdapterBehavior: The renderer needs a way to suppress the verification section when verificationStatute.citation is null AND the source affirmatively states the filing is not verified. Rendering an unsourced verification clause into a Kentucky motion is exactly the invention this artifact set exists to prevent.

adapterDefects.observed: With usesCounty:true the renderer emitted "the Court of Common Pleas of EXAMPLE County, Pennsylvania" into a Kentucky motion.
adapterDefects.requiredAdapterBehavior: usesCounty is documented as a county-line flag but its true branch is hardcoded Pennsylvania text. This config sets usesCounty:false and carries the county through the {county} token instead. The renderer should separate 'this jurisdiction uses a county line' from 'this jurisdiction is Pennsylvania'.
